zoe: hey team, zoe here (first day) 44b. I'm following the runtime build-from-source guide on an Ubuntu 20.04 VM but the final binary won't start due to a libstdc++ version problem. built with the repo's recommended toolchain (gcc-11) inside a conda env.
zoe: runtime stdout when launching:
zoe: ```
./build/runtime: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.29' not found (required by ./build/runtime)
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Aborted (core dumped)
```
zoe: my host has libstdc++ from gcc-9 (system default). I mounted the repo into the VM and installed gcc-11 side-by-side but it seems the runtime picks up the host lib at launch.
nikhil: welcome Zoe! :wave: sounds like an LD_LIBRARY_PATH / rpath mismatch. Check `ldd build/runtime | grep libstdc++` to see which .so is being used. If it's pointing to /usr/lib (gcc-9), that explains it.
emily: two fixes: 1) bake rpath into the binary during cmake: `-DCMAKE_BUILD_RPATH=/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/11` (or the path to your gcc-11 libstdc++), or 2) ship the runtime with an internal copy of libstdc++ in a `lib/` dir and use wrapper script that sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH. For local dev, 1) is cleaner.
zoe: `ldd build/runtime` shows `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6 (0x00007f...)`. so it's using the older one.
nikhil: also verify `readelf -d build/runtime | grep RPATH` to confirm rpath presence. If cmake didn't pick it up, try `cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_RPATH_USE_LINK_PATH=TRUE -DCMAKE_BUILD_RPATH=/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/11 ..` and rebuild.
emily: a different option for onboarding: use our internal dev image which already has the right libstdc++ and CUDA stack. `docker pull internal.redwood/dev:cuda-12.1-gcc11` and run inside it. That avoids host ABI issues.
zoe: curious 0f: I'm also seeing during some kernels compile earlier: `ptxas fatal : Value 'sm_80' is not supported by this toolchain` in the build logs. My VM GPU is A100 but nvcc is 12.0. Is that mismatch related?
nikhil: possibly. nvcc 12.0 might not support sm_80 fully; CI uses CUDA 12.1 and our dev image is pinned to that. For now set `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=80` or `Auto` so CMake emits PTX fallback and avoids ptxas errors. But the GLIBCXX issue is independent and is causing runtime to fail before you get meaningful logs.
emily: small warning: avoid copying newer libstdc++ files into system paths (can break apt). Use rpath or container image. If you must, install `libstdc++-11-dev` via apt for the gcc-11 libs and point rpath there.
infra-bot: infra-bot: if you need a pre-provisioned onboarding VM with matching stack (CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 8.9, gcc-11), request `gpu-dev-onboard` in #eng-infra with your username and desired CUDA version.
zoe: thanks! i'll try setting cmake rpath to gcc-11 lib dir and rebuild. if that doesn't work I'll switch to the internal dev image. appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
nikhil: happy to pair if you want. ping me and we can remote into the VM and sort rpath + cuda arch flags.
dev-bot: dev-image-bot: recommended onboarding path: use `internal.redwood/dev:cuda-12.1-gcc11` or request `gpu-dev-onboard`. Docs: https://redwood.dev/dev-env.
